Amaury Diaz Serrano.biografia_limpia: Amaury Diaz Serrano is a Puerto Rican-American industrial designer who was one of the six designers who participated in the Hot Wheels Designers Challenge; he represented General Motors's Chevrolet division, for he was Senior Industrial Designer, by designing the Chevroletor for said series, initially known as "Prototype 40". Diaz Serrano's dream was apparently to design a Hot Wheels car since he was a child. Diaz Serrano joined GM in 1999, working on numerous designs such as the exterior design of the Cadillac Sixteen; he left in 2015 and currently manages his own firm, Amaury Diaz Serrano Industrial Design LLC, as well as running Jigxocars, his other design firm. 1/64 Scale[] 1/64 Scale[] | Year | Casting Name | Debut Series | First Edition | Toy Number | Photo | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 2008 | GM Chevroletor | Designers Challenge | - | M3306 | | See also[] - Category:Amaury Diaz Serrano Designs

Lovejoy was a Hot Wheels designer who designed Hot Wheels from 1971 to 1973. He was hired alongside Larry Wood and Paul Tam as one of their earliest designers; he was most known for his work on the RRRumblers. Outside of work, Lovejoy was an aircraft enthusiast, building his own aircraft and gliders, most notably the Quicksilver; after he left Mattel he turned to solely developing aircraft and hang gliders. He worked his way up to become the director of the Hot Wheels engineering group before leaving Mattel entirely in 1989. Many of the innovative series such as X-V Racers, Steering Rigs, Crack-Ups, Flip Outs and the like can all be attributed to Rosas's work. Dave Deal David Allen Deal , nicknamed Big Deal , was an independent American illustrator who worked with Mattel in 2003, likely as a subcontractor. Born in 1938, Deal studied graphic design in Louisiana Tech University before becoming an illustrator for the Dallas Morning News; outside of that Deal was a notable illustrator, illustrating automobiles with "exaggerated" proportions, such as the _Deal's Wheels_ model kit line for Revell. Deal also set a record in a specially-modified Volkswagen Beetle on a 1000-mile route from Tijuana to La Paz alongside then-Revell product manager Don Ernst. Chris Colangelo.biografia_limpia: Harry Bradley Harry Bradley Tenure 1966 – 1969 Harry Bentley Bradley was an American automotive designer who is often considered the father of Hot Wheels designs; as Hot Wheels's very first designer, he created the original "Sweet 16" cars of 1968. Bradley worked for Mattel from 1966 to 1969. Born in Boston in 1936, Bradley suffered polio from a young age; despite this, he nurtured his talents drawing automobiles and continued sketching in hospitals as he received treatment for his condition. Prior to working for Hot Wheels, Bradley worked for General Motors, having been recruited in 1962, as well as being a builder of his own show cars such as the La Jolla, Blind Faith and the Deora . Bradley was recruited by Mattel in 1966, who wanted a designer from one of the Big 3 automakers to help design their vehicles. Bradley drove his 1964 Chevrolet El Camino to California; it is said that Mattel founder Elliot Handler saw Bradley's El Camino in the parking lot and quipped "Those are some hot wheels." Bradley's ties with GM were pivotal to the creation of some of the earliest Hot Wheels models. Lore has it that to design one of these GM models, the Custom Corvette , Bradley drove to Detroit in 1967 and snuck into GM's offices after working hours. ... Due to this it is often claimed the Hot Wheels version of the Corvette came out before the actual Corvette hit dealerships, much to GM's consternation, although various dating of prototypes and the corroboration of other dates states that this might not have been the case. Regardless, the Corvette was a highly popular model and caused great publicity for Mattel. Bradley left Mattel in 1969. The story behind how he left varies; some sources say he felt Hot Wheels would not take off and as such left the brand thinking it would only be a fad, while other sources say he was fired due to his refusal to be reassigned to the staples division of Ma
Chris Colangelo.bio: Christopher R. Colangelo is a Hot Wheels designer who has been working with Mattel since 2013. He is the design lead on the Hot Wheels Mario Kart series vehicles, Star Wars playsets, the Star Wars Starships line, design lead on San Diego Comic-Con exclusives and has worked on other major licenses for Hot Wheels, such as DC. Prior to his career at Mattel, he worked at Wham-O Toys, Jakks Pacific and Crayola and also had an internship career at Mattel before his full-time career.

Dave Deal.bio: David Allen Deal, nicknamed Big Deal, was an independent American illustrator who worked with Mattel in 2003, likely as a subcontractor. Born in 1938, Deal studied graphic design in Louisiana Tech University before becoming an illustrator for the Dallas Morning News; outside of that Deal was a notable illustrator, illustrating automobiles with "exaggerated" proportions, such as the Deal's Wheels model kit line for Revell. Deal also set a record in a specially-modified Volkswagen Beetle on a 1000-mile route from Tijuana to La Paz alongside then-Revell product manager Don Ernst. Deal passed away on 14 October 2008, aged 70, due to health problems; one of his last projects was concept art for the movie Cars.

Dave Martis.biografia_limpia: David A. Martis is a Hot Wheels designer, modelmaker, and prototyper who worked with Mattel from 1999 to late 2004 as a senior project designer and model maker. Known for his work on Mechanix, Robo Wheels, Gyro Jets, IR Rally, and 1/64 scale Disney/Pixar Cars prototypes, he preferred casting and hand painting “B-grade” resins using clay, SLA 3D prints, and existing parts from around the model shop as the process was “quicker and easier” than sketching concept art. It was stated by Eric Tscherne that his work features varying imperfections based off of the importance or purpose of each piece. He enjoyed casting and often made personal pieces that “blurred the line” between employee custom and prototype; many of his projects were used in presentations or eventual production releases. Many are marked with “X3008” on their bases; the “X” stood for "eXtension" to his office number “3008” to ensure their proper return after use. In years prior Martis designed bikes for GT Bicycles and automotive accessories for Powers Design International. After his tenure he worked at fellow toy company Playmates for a year, later founding his own company, Devium Design. 1/64 Scale[] 1/64 Scale[] | Year | Casting Name | Debut Series | First Edition | Toy Number | Photo | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 2001 | Honda Civic Si) | 2001 First Editions | 15/36 | 28758 | | | 2003 | Steel Flame | 2003 First Editions | 2/42 | 56354 | | | 2004 | Batmobile) | 2004 First Editions | 1/100 | B3540 | | See also[] - Category:Dave Martis Designs - [2000 Track Test (prototype)](/wi

Eligio Lee.bio: Eligio Lee es un diseñador surcoreano, ex empleado de Mattel que trabajó en la compañía alrededor de 2007. Durante su tiempo en Hot Wheels, diseñó el modelo Ultra Rage, un deportivo de batalla corta con elementos estilísticos de carreras que debutó en la serie New Models de 2007. Actualmente es el CEO de la sucursal de China y Hong Kong de CLO Virtual Fashion, una empresa especializada en software de diseño de moda 3D. Su paso por el equipo de diseño de Hot Wheels fue breve pero dejó un modelo reconocible en la línea mainline.

Felix Holst.bio: Felix C. Holst is a British designer who worked with Mattel's Hot Wheels division from 2004 to 2015 as the vice president of the creative division. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, Holst came to the United States some time after graduation and joined Mattel. He left Mattel in 2015 to found Hackrod Inc., a company specializing in vehicle design, which appears to have since closed. He is currently self-employed and is the founder of Holst Automotive; on the side, plays the bass guitar with a band called The Kustom Built and is a painter.

Fraser Campbell.biografia: Fraser Lee Campbell es un diseñador británico de Hot Wheels que trabajó en Mattel de 1998 a 2016 y nuevamente desde 2021. Inicialmente basado en el Reino Unido, Fraser se mudó a Estados Unidos en 2000 para unirse al equipo de diseño de Hot Wheels; su primer diseño fue Maelstrom. Se mudó a Hong Kong en algún momento posterior antes de regresar a Estados Unidos; gran parte de su trabajo durante su tiempo en Mattel involucró el diseño para Monster Jam y varios camiones para las líneas Truckin' Transporters, Pavement Pounders y relacionadas, así como algunas de las motocicletas de la línea Street Power. Campbell dejó Mattel a principios de 2016 para unirse a Hackrod, una empresa de diseño automotriz fundada por el ex vicepresidente de Diseño de Mattel y Hot Wheels, Felix Holst. Dejó Hackrod a mediados de 2020 y regresó a Mattel en 2021 como Líder de Proyecto de Diseño para Basics/Mainline.

Fraser Campbell.bio_en: Fraser Lee Campbell is a British Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 1998 to 2016 and again since 2021. Initially based in the UK, Fraser moved to the United States in 2000 to join the Hot Wheels design team; his first design was Maelstrom. He would move to Hong Kong at some point later before moving back to the United States; much of his work during his time at Mattel involved designing for Monster Jam and various haulers for Truckin' Transporters, Pavement Pounders and related lines as well as some of the bikes in the Street Power line. Campbell left Mattel in early 2016 to join Hackrod, an automotive design company started by ex-Mattel and Hot Wheels VP of Design Felix Holst. He left Hackrod in mid-2020 and returned to Mattel in 2021 as Lead Project designer for Basics/Mainline.

Harry Bradley.bio: Harry Bentley Bradley was an American automotive designer who is often considered the father of Hot Wheels designs; as Hot Wheels's very first designer, he created the original "Sweet 16" cars of 1968. Bradley worked for Mattel from 1966 to 1969. Born in Boston in 1936, Bradley suffered polio from a young age; despite this, he nurtured his talents drawing automobiles and continued sketching in hospitals as he received treatment for his condition. Prior to working for Hot Wheels, Bradley worked for General Motors, having been recruited in 1962, as well as being a builder of his own show cars such as the La Jolla, Blind Faith and the Deora. Bradley was recruited by Mattel in 1966, who wanted a designer from one of the Big 3 automakers to help design their vehicles. Bradley drove his 1964 Chevrolet El Camino to California; it is said that Mattel founder Elliot Handler saw Bradley's El Camino in the parking lot and quipped "Those are some hot wheels." Bradley's ties with GM were pivotal to the creation of some of the earliest Hot Wheels models. Lore has it that to design one of these GM models, the Custom Corvette, Bradley drove to Detroit in 1967 and snuck into GM's offices after working hours. Having worked in GM's design offices in the past, he was able to locate the area where the design blueprints were stored; he would take the blueprints for the upcoming 1968 Corvette by hiding them in his crutches, then drive back to California where he designed the model off those blueprints. Due to this it is often claimed the Hot Wheels version of the Corvette came out before the actual Corvette hit dealerships, much to GM's consternation, although various dating of prototypes and the corroboration of other dates states that this might not have been the case. Regardless, the Corvette was a highly popular model and caused great publicity for Mattel. Bradley left Mattel in 1969. The story behind how he left varies; some sources say he felt Hot Wheels would not take off and as such left the brand thinking it would only be a fad, while other sources say he was fired due to his refusal to be reassigned to the staples division of Mattel, with his manager fully convinced that the Hot Wheels line would fail. Others state that his firing might have been related to the aforementioned stunt he pulled regarding the Custom Corvette if indeed he did pull it off. This thought about failure held true for a time as Hot Wheels as a brand was not making any money with Mattel many a time considering retiring the brand and making numerous changes to cut costs, although in retrospect, he should have stayed and continued designing as the brand began turning a profit quickly during the mid 1970s. Prior to leaving Mattel, he recommended his friend Ira Gilford for the position, which the latter accepted. After leaving Mattel, Bradley started a design firm and did work on a number of projects. He then went on to become a lecturer at the Art Central College of Design, the institute from which many future Hot Wheels designers would graduate; he would also sporadically design new cars, with one of the last cars he did around the tail end of his "active period" being his "shark fin" 1993 Infiniti J30, although his last project was apparently a Pontiac he did for a friend circa 2010. Bradley passed away on 13 May 2023, aged 86.

Howard Rees.bio: Howard K. Rees is a former Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 1969 to 1975. Prior to his work at Mattel, he accepted a position at Ford of Europe. Rees left the Hot Wheels design team in 1971 to design the Major Matt Mason action figures, recommending a friend of his named Larry Wood to the position. Rees left Mattel entirely in 1975 and became a painter, which he still is to this day.

Ira Gilford.bio: Ira Bailey Gilford is a former Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 1967 to 1970. He is most known for designing a large number of the 1969 cars, The Spoilers, The Heavys and most notably, the Twin Mill, Hot Wheels's first original design. Prior to working for Mattel, Gilford worked for the Chrysler Corporation. Gilford was recommended to the position by his friend Harry Bradley, Hot Wheels's first designer. Gilford left Mattel around 1970. He currently works as an independent contractor in the digital arts field and a painter.

Ira Gilford.bio_en: Ira Gilford is recognized as the designer of the Twin Mill, the first original Hot Wheels design. He worked at Mattel from 1967 to 1970 and is considered one of the pioneers of the brand.

Jack Chen.bio: Jack Chen fue parte del equipo de diseño de Hot Wheels entre al menos 2003 y 2004. Durante este período diseñó varios modelos para las series First Editions, incluyendo el Corvette Stingray en 2003, el 1963 Corvette en 2004 y el Batmobile en 2004. Su estancia en Mattel fue relativamente corta pero contribuyó con reinterpretaciones de vehículos icónicos tanto del mundo del automóvil como de la cultura popular. Poco más se conoce sobre su trayectoria profesional fuera de su paso por Hot Wheels.

James Iida.biografia_limpia: James Iida is a Mattel employee who worked with Mattel from 2002 to 2010 and again since 2017. In his first tenure for Mattel, Iida was the lead designer for Hot Wheels "hard-line consumer products" and developed key arts for Hot Wheels style guides from 2006 to 2010. He also acted as a design for Sanrio Global, Disney Consumer Products, SA Studios Global and Saban Brands; he returned to Mattel in 2017 where he currently serves as a Lead Designer. 1/64 Scale
James Iida.bio: James Iida es un diseñador industrial que trabajó en Mattel desde 2002 hasta 2010 y luego regresó en 2017. Durante su primera etapa en Mattel, fue el diseñador principal de los hard-line consumer products de Hot Wheels y desarrolló key arts para las guías de estilo de Hot Wheels entre 2006 y 2010. También trabajó como diseñador para Sanrio Global, Disney Consumer Products, SA Studios Global y Saban Brands. Regresó a Mattel en 2017 donde actualmente se desempeña como Lead Designer. Entre sus diseños de hot wheels se encuentra el 1972 Plymouth Barracuda de la serie First Editions de 2004. Obtuvo su licenciatura en Diseño Industrial en la Universidad Estatal de California, Long Beach.

Register --- Sign In Advertisement Jun Imai is a Japanese-American former Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 2004 to 2018. Although his designs include classic American muscle cars and fantasy cars, he is most known for his Japanese cars. He has made replicas of his own 1:1 vehicles; the'71 Datsun Bluebird 510 Wagon, the Nissan Fairlady Z and the Datsun 620. He left Mattel in 2018 to work as a director of products at Roborace; he subsequently left Roborace in October 2020 and is currently working on a special series of cars with Hong Kong-based die-cast car company TrueScale Miniatures for their Mini GT line of high-detail 1:64 model automobiles. He worked as a Special Projects Manager for American electric car startup Canoo after leaving Roborace; he is currently the creative director of Kaido House, a company he founded selling automotive enthusiast merchandise; despite this he is still very active within the diecast community, making custom Hot Wheels cars which he sells and appearing at conventions. Jun Imai.bio: Jun Imai is a Japanese-American former Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 2004 to 2018. Although his designs include classic American muscle cars and fantasy cars, he is most known for his Japanese cars. He has made replicas of his own 1:1 vehicles; the '71 Datsun Bluebird 510 Wagon, the Nissan Fairlady Z and the Datsun 620. He left Mattel in 2018; he currently acts as the creative director of Kaido House, a company he founded selling automotive enthusiast merchandise and later morphing into a line of highly-detailed diecast cars manufactured in collaboration with TrueScale Miniatures and marketed as a subline to their Mini GT product line. His Kaido House brand also appeared on various Hot Wheels cars and he maintains a good relationship with his ex-colleagues.

Although his designs include classic American muscle cars and fantasy cars, he is most known for his Japanese cars. He has made replicas of his own 1:1 vehicles; the'71 Datsun Bluebird 510 Wagon, the Nissan Fairlady Z and the Datsun 620. He left Mattel in 2018 to work as a director of products at Roborace; he subsequently left Roborace in October 2020 and is currently working on a special series of cars with Hong Kong-based die-cast car company TrueScale Miniatures for their Mini GT line of high-detail 1:64 model automobiles. He worked as a Special Projects Manager for American electric car startup Canoo after leaving Roborace; he is currently the creative director of Kaido House, a company he founded selling automotive enthusiast merchandise; despite this he is still very active within the diecast community, making custom Hot Wheels cars which he sells and appearing at conventions. Leeway Chang.biografia_limpia: Leeway Chang Tenure 2007 – Present Title Staff Designer Signature Leeway Chang is a Hot Wheels staff designer specializing in graphics design who has worked at Mattel since 2007. Born in Taiwan, but spent most of his childhood in Latin America, Leeway traveled extensively before he settled in Southern California. Received his Associate of Arts degree in Communication Design from International Fine Arts College in Miami, Florida and Bachelor of Arts degree in Graphic Design from California State University Fullerton. Leeway designed graphics in the apparel, action sports, feature film, web, advertising and print for 17 years before joining Mattel in 2007. At Mattel, he was the lead Softline Designer for Boys Consumer Products for 5 years before moving over to the Wheels Packaging group as Staff Designer for Hot Wheels Adult Collector, RLC and Premium toy lines. Currently he is the graphic design lead for HW NFT projects, 5-Packs and Mystery packs. He also contributes to mainline basics as well. 1/64 Scale[] | Year | Casting Name | Debut Series | First Edition | Toy | Photo | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 2012 | Subaru WRX STI | 2012 New Models | 33/50 | V5321 | ](https://static.wiki
Leeway Chang.bio: Leeway Chang es un diseñador de planta de Hot Wheels especializado en diseño gráfico que trabaja en Mattel desde 2007. Nació en Taiwán pero pasó la mayor parte de su infancia en América Latina. Viajó extensamente antes de establecerse en el sur de California. Obtuvo un Associate of Arts en Communication Design del International Fine Arts College en Miami, Florida y un Bachelor of Arts en Graphic Design de la Universidad Estatal de California, Fullerton. Antes de unirse a Mattel, Leeway diseñó gráficos en la industria de la ropa, deportes de acción, cine, web, publicidad y print durante 17 años. En Mattel, fue el Softline Designer principal para Boys Consumer Products durante 5 años antes de pasar al grupo de empaquetado Wheels como Staff Designer para las líneas de juguetes Hot Wheels Adult Collector, RLC y Premium. Actualmente es el líder de diseño gráfico para proyectos de HW NFT, 5-Packs y Mystery packs, y también contribuye a los mainline basics. Entre sus diseños destacan Maximum Leeway, Subaru WRX STI, Lamborghini Sesto Elemento, Lamborghini Huracán y múltiples tampo designs para vehículos como el '70 Ford Escort RS1600.

This was her first job after graduating from the Art Center College of Design in 2015; prior to that, she interned at the Nissan Headquarter Studios in Tokyo. At Mattel she designed mainly for mainline, Premium and Extensions, as well as being in charge of designing retools for existing castings. Manson Cheung.bio: Manson Leo Cheungis a Hot Wheels 3D Modeler who has been working withMattelsince 2000. He is best known for his sculpting work (translating a designer's ideas and drawings into a three-dimensional prototype), but also designs and sculpts his own castings on occasion, usually from movies and the like. He is known on the Internet under his handle "awildermode", and is a well-known DeLorean enthusiast.

Matt Gabe.biografia_limpia: Matt Gabe Tenure 2009 – 2014 2018 – Present Title Manager, Hot Wheels Packaging Design Signature Matthew Wayne Gabe is a Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 2009 to 2014 and again since 2018. Prior to working at Mattel, he worked for competing brands Hasbro and Fisher-Price, mainly also as package designer. Mauricio Bedolla.bio: Mauricio Bedolla Gasca es un diseñador mexicano que trabajó en Mattel de 2005 a 2012. Fue también gerente de Matchbox. Su único casting conocido para Hot Wheels es el Scoopa Di Fuego, un supercoche futurista de estilo italiano que debutó en la serie New Models de 2010. El resto de su trabajo se centró principalmente en vehículos de la línea Matchbox. Actualmente trabaja como Design Manager para LEGO. Su paso por Hot Wheels fue breve pero el Scoopa Di Fuego se convirtió en una pieza de culto entre los coleccionistas.

Miguel López.biografia_limpia: Miguel Angel López Jr. is a Spanish-American Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 2012 to 2015, designing cars for both the Hot Wheels and Matchbox lines. He designed Hot Wheels cars such as the Fast 4WD and X-Steam, as well as a number of Star Wars and Disney Character Cars. He is currently a freelance artist, having been one since leaving Mattel, with his notable works now being a number of vehicles for the *Paw Patrol* line of toys manufactured by competing brand Spin Master. In addition to his work as an artist, López also worked as an English teacher from 2015 to 2017, first in Madrid, Spain and then later in Tokyo, Japan. Mike Nuttall.bio: Michael Wayne Nuttallis a former Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel's Hot Wheels division from 1999 to 2016; he mostly worked on designing track and playsets but occasionally designed vehicles, with his development on track sets leading him to be dubbed "Track Master Mike". He is decribed as "a master of toy design", he is stated to be able to whip out a "great concept sketch" faster than most people can pick up their pen. He is currently a member of InvenToy, a company started by former Hot Wheels engineersEric OstendorffandKeith Hippely. Prior to his stint at Hot Wheels, he worked for Mattel's Preschool division from 1970 to 1978 before moving to competing brand Tomy.

Register --- Sign In Advertisement Description 16 Angels is a futuristic V16-powered sports car. Inspiration for the car came from the Jaguar E-Type. Nathan Proch first thought about naming the car "E-go Type", but, wanting to avoid being called an ego maniac, changed the name to "Saturday Night Special". Legal put the kibosh on that one for obvious reasons. The eventual choice of "16 Angels" was for its cylinders, and, angels... (from Nathan Proch’s Heavenly Car, a Red Line Club exclusive article by HWC Gary): "I remember in Bible school when I was a kid, if I’m not mistaken, an angel has the power of 1,000 men or 10,000 men – they’re considered very strong in biblical terms." Nathan Proch The casting lost its metal body in 2009 and was retooled in 2015 to become a post-post design. Nathan Proch.bio: Nathan Clifford Prochis a former designer for Hot Wheels who worked at Mattel from 1993 to 2006; around that time he became debilitated with an unspecified illness which prevented him from working full time, and left soon after. Before his illness, Proch was responsible for the creation of theCM5wheel and the cut-out logos that appeared on the bases of Hot Wheels cars from 2005 to 2006. He also acted as Director of Hot Wheels Design for a time. Proch was inducted into the Diecast Hall of Fame in 2014 but declined the award; he has since kept a low profile.

Omar Rehman.bio: Omar Nayeemur Rehmanis a former Hot Wheels designer who interned at Mattel from June to December 2017. He designed both vehicles and smaller playsets. Prior to working at Mattel, Rehman interned at The Carlab and was PR for EuroJet Racing; after his stint at Hot Wheels he interned at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and worked as an industrial designer on contract with studio.VO and MODUS Group. He was last a communication designer for D-Ford, the Ford Motor Company's human-centric design group. He can be found on the internet under the handle @youknowitsomar.

Register --- Sign In Advertisement Otto Johnson Kuhni was a graphic artist that designed many the early art work for blisterpacks, cases and sets. Born in 1927 in Utah the fourth of five children, Kuhni began work as a freelance artist in 1962 and began work with Mattel in 1967, doing many of the drawings for card art and playsets; he even designed some large playsets himself. Kuhni retired in 1995, but returned part-time to do artwork for the then-new Hot Wheels Collectors series of cars, the accompanying Red Line Club and various other retro-themed products. Kuhni died in 2017, aged 90; his legacy lives in the form of his artwork as well as the Custom Otto, a rendition of the generic car he drew for the 1968 packaging artwork that was ultimately never released in the line and named in his honor. Quote from HW.com "Otto Kuhni has been a freelance designer with Mattel for over 45 years, and began working on Hot Wheels® cars in 1967. His first projects included designing art for the original blister card and many of the collector buttons, play sets and accessory packages for track, curves, jumps, loops and double loops. From 1968-1970, Kuhni also designed large play sets. Kuhni created the artwork used on many of the Hot Wheels® collector cases, including the 12-, 24, 48- and 72-car varieties. He also designed many of the Hot Wheels® blister card and collector set illustrations through 1995. He retired in 1995, but returned to work part-time for Mattel.and has been creating the illustrations for the HotWheelsCollectors.com cars and a new 12-car collector case." 1/64 Scale | Year | Casting Name | Debut Series | First Edition | Toy Number | Photo | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 2008 | Custom Otto | Toy Fair | - | M4681 | See also

Phil Riehlman.bio: Philip Oscar Riehlmanis a Hot Wheels designer that has been designing Hot Wheels cars since 1993. His first designs were theTwin Mill IIand theSilhouette IIas collaborations withBruce Baur; he also designed briefly for sister line Matchbox and currently also serves as a senior manager of Mattel. He was lead designer for theHot Wheels idline prior to its cancelation and currently designs models for Premium and the mainline; he is the lead designer forPremium 1:43andElite 64. He initially worked as an intern in 1991 before applying for a permanent position at the Male Action Figures department in 1993; he was subsequently transferred back to the Hot Wheels department, where he has been ever since.

Rob Matthes.bio: Robert William Matthes es un diseñador que trabajó en Hot Wheels de 2002 a 2017 y regresó en 2023. Es conocido como el diseñador líder de la línea Hot Wheels Elite a escala 1:18 y las líneas 1:50. Sirvió como gerente de diseño de Hot Wheels de 2008 a 2017, gestionando la línea de $1 de 2008 a 2012 y luego dirigiendo el equipo de playsets hasta su partida en 2017. También administra su propia empresa, SpeedShift Art, especializada en ilustración automotriz. Se unió a Mattel en 2002 y previamente fue Senior Industrial Designer en Herbst Lazar Bell, Chief Product Designer en Protective Technologies, Inc. (PTI) y Lead Designer/Manager en EDGE Product Development. Obtuvo su formación en el ArtCenter College of Design, la Universidad Estatal de California, Long Beach y UCLA. Regresó a Hot Wheels en 2023 trabajando principalmente en productos Premium. Entre sus numerosos diseños destacan el Batmobile (1989), Silhouette, Slikt Back, Splittin' Image, Toyota Celica, Wail Tale, Ford Bronco Concept, Formul8r, Hummer H3, Hummer H2, Preying Menace, Custom '62 Chevy, Bye Focal II, Custom V-8 Vega, Draggin' Tail, y múltiples Funny Cars de la serie Dragstrip Demons. También es conocido por su trabajo en los autos de Fórmula 1 de las líneas Basic y Premium. Durante su gestión como gerente de diseño, aumentó las ventas un 20% anual en mercados emergentes, redujo el tiempo de desarrollo un 40% y lideró el equipo que recibió el premio al juguete más vendido de Mattel en la temporada navideña de 2015.

After graduating, he initially began work as a designer for Matchbox from 2004 to 2012; he first designed for Hot Wheels in 2009 as a "guest designer", and would join the Hot Wheels design team three years later. He passed away on 23 March 2021 at the age of 42 from cancer. Scott Robertson.biografia_limpia: Scott Robertson Scott Robertson is a designer who designed cars for Hot Wheels in 2005; he did not actually work for Mattel during that time however. Robertson is an educator on the side, teaching initially at the Art Center College of Design from 1995 to 2010 and then from his own company, Scott Robertson Design LLC. He authored the book *How To Draw Cars The Hot Wheels Way* with assistance from the Hot Wheels design team. In addition to designing, he also builds hot rods; his custom 1934 Ford Pickup, "FORDTRUSS", won the El Segundo leg of the 2024 Hot Wheels Legends Tour. 1/64 Scale

He also worked on Dropstars, Dropstars Urban Assault Vehicles, Custom Classics, Hot Import Nights and HIN D-Force models. Steve Gilmore.bio: Steven Gilmore is an American automotive designer who was one of the six designers who participated in the Hot Wheels Designers Challenge; he represented the Ford Motor Company, for he was Design Manager of Ford, by designing the Ford Gangster Grin for said series. Gilmore has been with Ford since 2000, and is one of two Designers Challenge designers with ties to Hot Wheels before going onto professional design; he interned at Mattel for four months in 1998 during college. He is currently Design Chief of Vehicle Personalization at Ford.

Steve Moran.bio: Steven M. Moranis a former Hot Wheels designer who worked at the company from 1997 to 2011. Moran was first asked to direct the Hong Kong Hot Wheels design team in 1997, and became a senior design manager in 2000. He worked with Hot Wheels mainly managing the direction of the Hot Wheels Elite line among other lines and left the design team in 2008 to work for another division of Mattel. Moran left Mattel entirely in 2011 and went to work for Jada Toys; he also founded Moran Devices LLC the same year. Moran returned to Mattel as a "mentor project lead" in 2012 and left in 2015.

Terry Choy.bio: Terence Allan Choywas a Chinese-American toy designer who designed for Mattel from1984to 2005. He started as Senior Designer (1984-1985), Project Designer (1985-1987), then Senior Project Designer (1988-2005). He was the Project Manager for the Adult/Collector Division of Hot Wheels Racing, which included Formula 1, NASCAR and Rally products. He was responsible for the earliest Batmobile casting designs for Hot Wheels with the 100% Batmobiles Series which debuted in 2003 with the Dream Halloween 1989 Batmobile; made for charity. He was a designer forThe Simpsonstoy line in addition to his Hot Wheels portfolio. He was one of the designers for some of the vehicles for an ill-fatedHe Manmovie, alongside a number of other Hot Wheels designers. Terry passed away on 7 April 2020 from cancer, aged 67.

Todd Gibbs.bio: Todd Gibbs es un diseñador que trabajó en Mattel de 2012 a 2015. Durante su tiempo en Hot Wheels, fue el diseñador principal de la línea The Muppets Character Cars y del modelo Tarmac Attack. Antes de Mattel, Gibbs estudió en el ArtCenter College de Diseño y acumuló una amplia experiencia en desarrollo visual y diseño de productos. Dejó Mattel en 2015 y desde entonces ha trabajado en estudios de animación y entretenimiento como DreamWorks Animation, Sony Pictures Animation y Warner Bros., contribuyendo a películas como Hotel Transylvania 2, Puss In Boots, Turbo y Rise of the Guardians como artista de visual development. Actualmente es Director Creativo especializado en experiencias de producto interactivo. También fue diseñador de productos senior en Spin Master y LEGO antes de su paso por Mattel.

Tony Martino.bio: Anthony M. Martino, conocido como Tony Martino, es un diseñador de Hot Wheels que trabaja para Mattel desde al menos 2006. Se especializa principalmente en la línea de Hot Wheels Monster Trucks, para la que ha diseñado numerosos vehículos temáticos con licencias. Entre sus diseños destacan Vintage Grave Digger, Iron Man, Spider-Man, Kool Kombi, Renault 5 Turbo, So Plowed, Bone Shaker, Dairy Delivery, Hound Hauler, Stone Cold Steve Austin, Undertaker, Abyss-Mal, Bad Cattitude, Bowser, Krang, Milk Monster, Patrick, RingMaster, 1 Bad Scoop, HW Pizza Co., Tyrannosaurus Rex, Collision Crusher y Wild Wrecker. Su trabajo abarca colaboraciones con franquicias como Monster Jam, WWE, Super Mario, SpongeBob SquarePants, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles y Jurassic World.

York Bleyer.biografia_limpia: York H. Bleyer is a former Hot Wheels designer and design manager who worked at Mattel from 2007 to 2011. Prior to working at Mattel, he was an industrial designer, working with numerous companies before moving to Mattel in 2007. Initially working with Tyco, York moved to Hot Wheels in 2011 where he managed various employees and led the Innovation Small Vehicles and Track and Playsets team, in addition to contributing to some design work. Projects he contributed to during his tenure at Hot Wheels include Stealth Rides, Wall Tracks, Batman, Cars, Toy Story, Green Lantern, Speed Racer and Max Steel playsets. After his tenure at Mattel he worked for Ridemakerz and ran his own design studio, and was last an adjunct professor at the Academy of Art University. Driving through the streets of San Francisco provided its challenges but confirmed his belief that a motorcycle was the perfect tool for commuting in the city. He has used this form of transportation for commuting to work in New York City, Detroit and Troy Michigan to the greater Los Angeles Southern California area. Riding bikes has remained his favorite way to travel to this day. 1/64 Scale[] 1/64 Scale[] | Year | Casting Name | Debut Series | First Edition | Toy Number | Photo | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 2011 | Volkswagen Brasília | 2011 New Models | 8/50 | T9678 | | | 2012 | '76 Chevy Monza | The Hot Ones) | - | W3775 | | Gallery[] See also[] - His website (defunct) - Category:York Bleyer Designs

Paul Tam.bio_es: Paul Tam soñó toda su vida con diseñar autos para General Motors. Hizo realidad ese sueño en los años 60, aunque duró poco. En 1970, condujo hasta California, a las oficinas de Mattel, y dijo: Quiero un trabajo. Se unió a Larry Wood e Ira Gilford en Mattel en los primeros días de Hot Wheels como diseñador y comenzó a diseñar algunos de los autos emblemáticos de la empresa. Entre ellos, el Whip Creamer, un auto de turbina, que fue su primer diseño para Hot Wheels. Tam trabajó para Mattel hasta 1973. Entre los muchos diseños futuristas se incluyen Evil Weevil, Open Fire, Six Shooter y el raro Double Header (co-diseñado con Larry Wood). A los 63 años, Paul Tam dirige un negocio de financiamiento en su natal Sudáfrica.
Paul Tam.bio_en: Paul Tam's lifelong dream was to design cars for General Motors. He joined Larry Wood and Ira Gilford at Mattel in the early days of Hot Wheels, designing signature cars including the Whip Creamer, Evil Weevil, Open Fire, Six Shooter, and Double Header. He worked for Mattel until 1973.

Ed Watts.biografia_limpia: Ed Watts was a Hot Wheels employee who worked for Mattel from the 1980s to the early 2000s; he is known to have worked on Masters of the Universe figures as well as the Top Speed line of Hot Wheels cars. He retired in 2002 due to a stage 4 brain tumor diagnosis, with the Ed Watts Race Team Red Line Club set created to honor him; all the proceeds from the set would go to Watts's family. He unfortunately lost his battle with cancer some time later.

Ronald Wong.biografia_limpia: Ronald Wong is a Hong Kong Hot Wheels designer who has worked with Mattel since 2014, initially as an intern before joining Mattel full-time as a Product Designer; he currently manages the Hot Wheels Premium line. He is noted to prioritize track performance for his designs; many of his designs are noted to be of high-end exotic cars. In addition to cars, he has designed a number of larger-scale vehicles and track sets. In addition to his design work at Mattel, Wong is also a photographer, photographing Hong Kong's car culture; he is also a collector of Hot Wheels and other larger scale diecast models, having maintained a collection since his childhood. He can be found under the internet handle ronalderw.

He is currently the senior vice-president and global head of design, vehicles and building sets, a position he has held since 2024.

Leo Zugner.biografia_limpia: Leo Zugner is an industrial designer who worked at Mattel from 2012 to 2019. He was involved with the Hot Wheels Advanced Play department, designing new products for Hot Wheels's future of play. He is known for the design of some Sky Busters models and the Hot Wheels id line, particularly the loop section in the Smart Track Kit as well as the Race Portal. Prior to joining Mattel, he was a designer for competing brand Jakks Pacific as well as Future Elements and Lanard Toys. He currently works at Salient Technologies.

Neal Smith.biografia_limpia: Neal Thomas Smith es un exdiseñador de Hot Wheels que trabajó en Mattel de 2013 a 2023, ocupando finalmente el cargo de Senior/Lead Product Designer. Principalmente ayudó en el desarrollo de varios sets de pistas y juegos, asistió con el lanzamiento de las series Minecraft, Monster Trucks y Skate, así como con prototipos y otros trabajos a mayor escala. Neal también ha estado a cargo de la creación de modelos a escala 1/64 y liveries en ocasiones. Es conocido por usar los seudónimos 'NEEEL' y 'Dr. Neeel' en sus redes sociales. Actualmente trabaja en Buck Knives como Especialista en Diseño Industrial.
Neal Smith.bio_es: Neal Thomas Smith es un exdiseñador de Hot Wheels que trabajó en Mattel de 2013 a 2023, ocupando finalmente el cargo de Senior/Lead Product Designer. Principalmente ayudó en el desarrollo de varios sets de pistas y juegos, asistió con el lanzamiento de las series Minecraft, Monster Trucks y Skate, así como con prototipos y otros trabajos a mayor escala. Neal también ha estado a cargo de la creación de modelos a escala 1/64 y liveries en ocasiones. Es conocido por usar los seudónimos 'NEEEL' y 'Dr. Neeel' en sus redes sociales. Actualmente trabaja en Buck Knives como Especialista en Diseño Industrial.
Neal Smith.bio_en: Neal Thomas Smith is a former Hot Wheels designer who worked with Mattel from 2013 to 2023 and last held the position of Senior/Lead Product Designer. He has primarily aided in the development of various track and play sets, assisted with the launch of the Minecraft, Monster Trucks, and Skate series, as well as some prototyping and other work for larger scale series. Neal has been tasked with the creation of 1/64 scale models and liveries on occasion. He is known for using the pseudonyms 'NEEEL' and 'Dr. Neeel' on his public social media accounts. He currently works at Buck Knives as an Industrial Design Specialist.
Neal Smith.bio_pt: Neal Thomas Smith é um ex-designer da Hot Wheels que trabalhou na Mattel de 2013 a 2023, ocupando por último o cargo de Sênior/Líder de Designer de Produto. Ele ajudou principalmente no desenvolvimento de vários conjuntos de pistas e brinquedos, auxiliou no lançamento das séries Minecraft, Monster Trucks e Skate, além de alguns protótipos e outros trabalhos para séries em maior escala. Neal também foi encarregado da criação de modelos em escala 1/64 e liveries em ocasiões. Ele é conhecido por usar os pseudônimos 'NEEEL' e 'Dr. Neeel' em suas contas públicas de mídia social. Atualmente trabalha na Buck Knives como Especialista em Design Industrial.
Neal Smith.bio_fr: Neal Thomas Smith est un ancien designer Hot Wheels qui a travaillé chez Mattel de 2013 à 2023 et a occupé le poste de Senior/Lead Product Designer. Il a principalement contribué au développement de divers circuits et sets de jeu, a assisté au lancement des séries Minecraft, Monster Trucks et Skate, ainsi qu'à certains prototypes et autres travaux pour des séries à plus grande échelle. Neal a également été chargé de la création de modèles à l'échelle 1/64 et de liveries à l'occasion. Il est connu pour utiliser les pseudonymes 'NEEEL' et 'Dr. Neeel' sur ses comptes de médias sociaux publics. Il travaille actuellement chez Buck Knives en tant que Spécialiste en Design Industriel.

Eric So.biografia_limpia: Eric So Kar-Fai es un empleado de Mattel con sede en Hong Kong que trabaja en Mattel desde 1994; diseña principalmente playsets. Antes de su etapa en Mattel, trabajó durante varios años en varias empresas de diseño de juguetes con sede en Hong Kong. Trabajó en El Segundo durante aproximadamente un año en 2004. En Hong Kong, es apodado la 'impresora humana'.
Eric So.bio_es: Eric So Kar-Fai es un empleado de Mattel con sede en Hong Kong que trabaja en Mattel desde 1994; diseña principalmente playsets. Antes de su etapa en Mattel, trabajó durante varios años en varias empresas de diseño de juguetes con sede en Hong Kong. Trabajó en El Segundo durante aproximadamente un año en 2004. En Hong Kong, es apodado la 'impresora humana'.
Eric So.bio_en: Eric So Kar-Fai is a Mattel employee based in Hong Kong who has been working at Mattel since 1994; he mainly designs playsets. Prior to his stint at Mattel, he worked for a number of small Hong Kong-based toy design companies for a number of years before making the switch. He worked at El Segundo for about a year in 2004. Within Hong Kong, he is nicknamed the 'human printer'.
Eric So.bio_pt: Eric So Kar-Fai é um funcionário da Mattel com sede em Hong Kong que trabalha na Mattel desde 1994; ele principalmente cria playsets. Antes de sua passagem pela Mattel, ele trabalhou por várias empresas de design de juguetes de sede em Hong Kong por vários anos. Trabalhou em El Segundo por cerca de um ano em 2004. Em Hong Kong, é apelidado de 'impressora humana'.
Eric So.bio_fr: Eric So Kar-Fai est un employé de Mattel basé à Hong Kong qui travaille chez Mattel depuis 1994 ; il conçoit principalement des playsets. Avant son passage chez Mattel, il a travaillé pendant plusieurs années dans plusieurs petites entreprises de design de jouets basées à Hong Kong. Il a travaillé à El Segundo pendant environ un an en 2004. À Hong Kong, il est surnommé 'l'imprimante humaine'.

George Soulakis.biografia_limpia: George Soulakis Jr. fue un diseñador e ingeniero de Hot Wheels que trabajó en Mattel de 1968 a 2000. Fue el principal ingeniero y diseñador detrás de los Sizzlers. También sugirió a Mattel utilizar el proceso de tampografía para aplicar gráficos suavemente en la superficie de los Hot Wheels en 1972; Mattel gastó más de $100,000 en la compra del equipo necesario para el proceso, lo que finalmente resultó un éxito ya que los tampos se han utilizado en los autos Hot Wheels desde entonces. Soulakis se jubiló de Mattel en 2000. Falleció el 6 de junio de 2025, a los 89 años.
George Soulakis.bio_es: George Soulakis Jr. fue un diseñador e ingeniero de Hot Wheels que trabajó en Mattel de 1968 a 2000. Fue el principal ingeniero y diseñador detrás de los Sizzlers. También sugirió a Mattel utilizar el proceso de tampografía para aplicar gráficos suavemente en la superficie de los Hot Wheels en 1972; Mattel gastó más de $100,000 en la compra del equipo necesario para el proceso, lo que finalmente resultó un éxito ya que los tampos se han utilizado en los autos Hot Wheels desde entonces. Soulakis se jubiló de Mattel en 2000. Falleció el 6 de junio de 2025, a los 89 años.
George Soulakis.bio_en: George Soulakis Jr. was a Hot Wheels designer and engineer who was employed with Mattel from 1968 to 2000. He was the main engineer and designer behind the Sizzlers. He also suggested to Mattel to use the Tampoprint process to smoothly applying graphics on the surface of Hot Wheels in 1972; Mattel spent over $100,000 purchasing the various equipment required for the process, which ultimately was a successful venture as tampos have been used on Hot Wheels cars since. Soulakis retired from Mattel in 2000. Soulakis passed away on 6 June 2025, aged 89.
George Soulakis.bio_pt: George Soulakis Jr. foi um designer e engenheiro da Hot Wheels que trabalhou na Mattel de 1968 a 2000. Ele foi o principal engenheiro e designer por trás dos Sizzlers. Também sugeriu à Mattel usar o processo de tampografia para aplicar gráficos suavemente na superfície dos Hot Wheels em 1972; a Mattel gastou mais de $100.000 comprando os equipamentos necessários para o processo, o que acabou sendo um sucesso, já que os tampos são usados nos carros Hot Wheels desde então. Soulakis aposentou-se da Mattel em 2000. Faleceu em 6 de junho de 2025, aos 89 anos.
George Soulakis.bio_fr: George Soulakis Jr. était un designer et ingénieur Hot Wheels qui a travaillé chez Mattel de 1968 à 2000. Il était le principal ingénieur et designer derrière les Sizzlers. Il a également suggéré à Mattel d'utiliser le processus de tampographie pour appliquer des graphiques en douceur sur la surface des Hot Wheels en 1972 ; Mattel a dépensé plus de 100 000 $ pour l'achat de l'équipement nécessaire au processus, ce qui a finalement été un succès puisque les tampons sont utilisés sur les voitures Hot Wheels depuis lors. Soulakis a pris sa retraite de Mattel en 2000. Il est décédé le 6 juin 2025, à l'âge de 89 ans.

Gary Swisher.biografia_limpia: Gary Ronald Swisher es un exempleado de Mattel que trabajó en Mattel de 1990 a 2018 en su división de Hot Wheels. Su último puesto fue el de Vicepresidente de Relaciones con Inventores en Mattel, cargo que ocupó desde 2005 hasta su salida. Actualmente trabaja como Vicepresidente Ejecutivo de Diseño en la marca competidora Spin Master.

Gary Swisher.bio_en: Gary Ronald Swisher is a former Mattel employee who worked with Mattel from 1990 to 2018 in their Hot Wheels division. He last held the post of Vice President for Inventor Relations in Mattel, a position he held from 2005 until his departure. He currently works as an Executive Vice President of Design at competing brand Spin Master.
Gary Swisher.bio_pt: Gary Ronald Swisher é um ex-funcionário da Mattel que trabalhou na Mattel de 1990 a 2018 em sua divisão Hot Wheels. Atualmente trabalha como Vice-Presidente Executivo de Design na marca concorrente Spin Master.
Gary Swisher.bio_fr: Gary Ronald Swisher est un ancien employé de Mattel qui a travaillé chez Mattel de 1990 à 2018 dans sa division Hot Wheels. Il a occupé pour dernier poste celui de Vice-Président des Relations avec les Inventeurs chez Mattel, poste qu'il a occupé de 2005 jusqu'à son départ. Il travaille actuellement comme Vice-Président Exécutif du Design chez la marque concurrente Spin Master.

Alton Takeyasu.biografia_limpia: Alton Takeyasu es un diseñador industrial que ha trabajado con Mattel desde 1991. Antes de trabajar en Mattel, fue diseñador en Kenner Toys de 1984 a 1991. Takeyasu fue responsable de todas las propiedades basadas en entretenimiento con licencia y las propiedades intelectuales desarrolladas internamente producidas por Mattel, y también estuvo involucrado en el diseño de varios autos Hot Wheels a tamaño completo, así como en varias líneas de figuras de acción.

Alton Takeyasu.bio_en: Alton Takeyasu is an industrial designer who has worked with Mattel since 1991. Prior to working at Mattel, he was a designer at Kenner Toys from 1984 to 1991. Takeyasu was responsible for all licensed entertainment-based properties and internally-developed intellectual properties produced by Mattel and was also involved in the design of various full-sized Hot Wheels car designs as well as various lines of action figures.
Alton Takeyasu.bio_pt: Alton Takeyasu é um designer industrial que trabalha com a Mattel desde 1991. Antes de trabalhar na Mattel, foi designer na Kenner Toys de 1984 a 1991. Takeyasu foi responsável por todas as propriedades licenciadas baseadas em entretenimento e propriedades intelectuais desenvolvidas internamente produzidas pela Mattel, e também esteve envolvido no design de vários carros Hot Wheels em tamanho real, bem como várias linhas de figuras de ação.
Alton Takeyasu.bio_fr: Alton Takeyasu est un designer industriel qui travaille avec Mattel depuis 1991. Avant de travailler chez Mattel, il était designer chez Kenner Toys de 1984 à 1991. Takeyasu était responsable de toutes les propriétés sous licence basées sur le divertissement et des propriétés intellectuelles développées en interne produites par Mattel, et a également participé à la conception de plusieurs voitures Hot Wheels grandeur nature ainsi que de diverses lignes de figurines d'action.

Alec Tam.biografia_limpia: Alec Paul Tam es un exdiseñador de Hot Wheels chino-estadounidense y el único diseñador de Hot Wheels de segunda generación que trabajó en Mattel de 2000 a 2018. Siguiendo los pasos de su padre, Paul Tam, Alec ha tenido un gran impacto en la marca, donde fue Director de Diseño para la línea principal. Alec rediseñó uno de los autos de su padre, el Whip Creamer, que consiguió un gran número de seguidores entre los coleccionistas. Alec se unió a Mattel en 2000 inicialmente como diseñador de proyectos para Hot Wheels y ocupó varios puestos antes de convertirse en Director de Diseño de Vehículos en 2007. En 2012, se convirtió en director senior de diseño de productos de Wheels Brands, cargo que ocupó hasta 2013. Subsequently became a design consultant for toy brands such as Moose Toys and is currently Director of Global Product Development for toys at MerchSource.
Alec Tam.bio_es: Alec Paul Tam es un exdiseñador de Hot Wheels chino-estadounidense y el único diseñador de Hot Wheels de segunda generación que trabajó en Mattel de 2000 a 2018. Siguiendo los pasos de su padre, Paul Tam, Alec ha tenido un gran impacto en la marca, donde fue Director de Diseño para la línea principal. Alec rediseñó uno de los autos de su padre, el Whip Creamer, que consiguió un gran número de seguidores entre los coleccionistas. Alec se unió a Mattel en 2000 inicialmente como diseñador de proyectos para Hot Wheels y ocupó varios puestos antes de convertirse en Director de Diseño de Vehículos en 2007. En 2012, se convirtió en director senior de diseño de productos de Wheels Brands, cargo que ocupó hasta 2013. Subsequently became a design consultant for toy brands such as Moose Toys and is currently Director of Global Product Development for toys at MerchSource.
Alec Tam.bio_en: Alec Paul Tam is a Chinese-American former Hot Wheels designer and the only second generation Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 2000 to 2018. Following in the footsteps of his father, Paul Tam, Alec has made a huge impact on the brand where he was the Director of Design for the mainline. Alec redesigned one of his father's cars, the Whip Creamer, which went on to garner a sizable following amongst collectors. Alec joined Mattel in 2000 initially as a project designer for Hot Wheels and moved around a few times before becoming the Director of Vehicle Design in 2007. In 2012, he became the senior director of product design of Wheels Brands, a position he held until 2013, at which point he moved out of the department and to Boys Entertainment; his last known position at Mattel was a Director for Girls's Product Design. He subsequently became a design consultant for a number of toy brands such as Moose Toys before being employed at YULU Toys; he is currently a Director for Global Product Development for toys at MerchSource.
Alec Tam.bio_pt: Alec Paul Tam é um ex-designer Hot Wheels chinês-americano e o único designer Hot Wheels de segunda geração que trabalhou na Mattel de 2000 a 2018. Seguindo os passos de seu pai, Paul Tam, Alec teve um grande impacto na marca, onde foi Diretor de Design para a linha principal. Alec redesenhou um dos carros de seu pai, o Whip Creamer, que conquistou um número considerável de seguidores entre colecionadores. Alec ingressou na Mattel em 2000 inicialmente como designer de projetos para Hot Wheels e mudou várias vezes antes de se tornar Diretor de Design de Veículos em 2007. Em 2012, tornou-se diretor sênior de design de produtos da Wheels Brands, cargo que ocupou até 2013, quando saiu do departamento e foi para Boys Entertainment; seu último cargo conhecido na Mattel foi Diretor de Design de Produtos para Meninas. Subsequentemente tornou-se consultor de design para marcas de brinquedos como a Moose Toys e atualmente é Diretor de Desenvolvimento Global de Produtos para brinquedos na MerchSource.
Alec Tam.bio_fr: Alec Paul Tam est un ancien designer Hot Wheels sino-américain et le seul designer Hot Wheels de deuxième génération qui a travaillé chez Mattel de 2000 à 2018. Suivant les traces de son père, Paul Tam, Alec a eu un impact énorme sur la marque où il était Directeur du Design pour la ligne principale. Alec a redessiné l'une des voitures de son père, le Whip Creamer, qui a réussi à rassembler un nombre considérable d'adeptes parmi les collectionneurs. Alec a rejoint Mattel en 2000 initialement en tant que designer de projet pour Hot Wheels et a occupé plusieurs postes avant de devenir Directeur du Design Véhicule en 2007. En 2012, il est devenu directeur senior du design de produits de Wheels Brands, poste qu'il a occupé jusqu'en 2013, date à laquelle il a quitté le département pour rejoindre Boys Entertainment ; son dernier poste connu chez Mattel était Directeur du Design de Produits pour Filles. Il est ensuite devenu consultant en design pour plusieurs marques de jouets telles que Moose Toys avant d'être employé chez YULU Toys ; il est actuellement Directeur du Développement de Produits Mondiaux pour jouets chez MerchSource.

Mark Trageser.biografia_limpia: Mark Trageser es un exdiseñador de Hot Wheels que trabajó en Mattel de 2000 a 2006. Es conocido por haber sido uno de los diseñadores detrás de la serie Formula Fuelers, así como por haber trabajado en la serie Speed Readerz. Actualmente trabaja para JMP Creative como diseñador y especialista en impresión 3D, y es el fundador de dos empresas de juguetes con sede en Los Ángeles: InsaniTOY y Kram-Co 3D.
Mark Trageser.bio_es: Mark Trageser es un exdiseñador de Hot Wheels que trabajó en Mattel de 2000 a 2006. Mark Trageser.bio_en: Mark Trageser is a former Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 2000 to 2006. He is currently working for JMP Creative as a designer and 3D printing specialist and the founder of two Los Angeles-based toy companies; InsaniTOY and Kram-Co 3D.
Mark Trageser.bio_pt: Mark Trageser é um ex-designer da Hot Wheels que trabalhou na Mattel de 2000 a 2006. Mark Trageser.bio_fr: Mark Trageser est un ancien designer Hot Wheels qui a travaillé chez Mattel de 2000 à 2006. Il est connu pour avoir été l'un des designers derrière la série Formula Fuelers, ainsi que pour avoir travaillé sur la série Speed Readerz. Il travaille actuellement pour JMP Creative en tant que designer et spécialiste de l'impression 3D et est le fondateur de deux entreprises de jouets basées à Los Angeles : InsaniTOY et Kram-Co 3D.

Eric Tscherne.biografia_limpia: Eric C. Tscherne fue incluido en el Salón de la Fama Diecast en 2011 y fue diseñador de Hot Wheels de 1998 a 2004. Es más conocido por introducir muchos de los autos tuner de importación. También desarrolló diseños originales realistas como Muscle Tone, 40 Somethin' y Switchback. Los originales de estilo realista y el tema de revisitación del pasado eran algo en lo que creía y ayudaron a hacer un sello de la línea. Tscherne también es recordado por crear la línea Hot Tunerz, que llevó a muchos de los autos 'Tooned, Fatbax y los impopulares Hardnoze. Más tarde, Tscherne diseñó autos y juguetes para Jada Toys (Chub City, Dub City, Import Racer, Big Time Muscle) y creó la línea JL Full Throttle. También se le atribuye la supervisión del rediseño de la marca Johnny Lightning. Más tarde trabajó para Wicked Cool Toys como director senior de diseño. Actualmente trabaja para Ultra Cornhole como diseñador de indumentaria y tiene su propia empresa, ET Design.
Eric Tscherne.bio_es: Eric C. Tscherne fue incluido en el Salón de la Fama Diecast en 2011 y fue diseñador de Hot Wheels de 1998 a 2004. Es más conocido por introducir muchos de los autos tuner de de importación. También desarrolló diseños originales realistas como Muscle Tone, 40 Somethin' y Switchback. Los originales de estilo realista y el tema de revisitación del pasado eran algo en lo que creía y ayudaron a hacer un sello de la línea. Tscherne también es recordado por crear la línea Hot Tunerz, que llevó a muchos de los autos 'Tooned, Fatbax y los impopulares Hardnoze. Más tarde, Tscherne diseñó autos y juguetes para Jada Toys (Chub City, Dub City, Import Racer, Big Time Muscle) y creó la línea JL Full Throttle. También se le atribuye la supervisión del rediseño de la marca Johnny Lightning. Más tarde trabajó para Wicked Cool Toys como director senior de diseño. Actualmente trabaja para Ultra Cornhole como diseñador de indumentaria y tiene su propia empresa, ET Design.
Eric Tscherne.bio_en: Eric C. Tscherne is a 2011 Inductee of the Diecast Hall of Fame and was a Hot Wheels Designer from 1998 through 2004. He is best known for ushering in many of the import tuner type cars. He also developed realistic original designs like Muscle Tone, 40 Somethin' and Switchback. The realistically styled originals and the theme of revisiting past cars were both something he believed in and help make a staple of the line. Other designers continue to follow in this tradition. Tscherne also is remembered for creating the Hot Tunerz line which led to many of the 'Tooned, Fatbax and the poorly received Hardnoze styled cars. Tscherne went on to design cars and toys for Jada Toys (Chub City, Dub City, Import Racer, Big Time Muscle) and created the JL Full Throttle line, featuring Designs from Chip Foose and TLC's Overhaulin'. He is also credited with overseeing the redesign of Johnny Lightning's brand look, creating its current retro-cool theme for RC2/Learning Curve. He was later employed for Wicked Cool Toys, where he acted as a senior director of design designing vehicles for lines such as Paw Patrol. He is currently employed for Ultra Cornhole as an apparel designer, with whom he also plays competitive cornhole; he also has his own company, ET Design.
Eric Tscherne.bio_pt: Eric C. Tscherne é um integrante de 2011 do Diecast Hall of Fame e foi Designer da Hot Wheels de 1998 a 2004. Ele é mais conhecido por introduzir muitos dos carros tuner de importação. Também desenvolveu designs realistas originais como Muscle Tone, 40 Somethin' e Switchback. Os originais de estilo realista e o tema de revisitar carros do passado eram algo em que ele acreditava e ajudaram a tornar um marco da linha. Outros designers continuam seguindo essa tradição. Tscherne também é lembrado por criar a linha Hot Tunerz, que levou a muitos dos carros 'Tooned, Fatbax e os impopulares Hardnoze. Tscherne passou a projetar carros e brinquedos para a Jada Toys (Chub City, Dub City, Import Racer, Big Time Muscle) e criou a linha JL Full Throttle. Ele também é creditado por supervisionar o redesign da marca Johnny Lightning. Mais tarde, trabalhou para a Wicked Cool Toys como diretor sênior de design. Atualmente trabalha para a Ultra Cornhole como designer de vestuário e tem sua própria empresa, ET Design.
Eric Tscherne.bio_fr: Eric C. Tscherne est un membre 2011 du Diecast Hall of Fame et a été Designer Hot Wheels de 1998 à 2004. Il est surtout connu pour avoir introduit de nombreuses voitures tuner importées. Il a également développé des designs réalistes originaux comme Muscle Tone, 40 Somethin' et Switchback. Les originaux au style réaliste et le thème du retour aux voitures du passé étaient quelque chose en quoi il croyait et ont contribué à faire une marque de fabrique de la ligne. D'autres designers continuent de suivre cette tradition. Tscherne est également rappelé pour avoir créé la ligne Hot Tunerz qui a conduit à de nombreuses voitures 'Tooned, Fatbax et les impopulaires Hardnoze. Tscherne a ensuite conçu des voitures et des jouets pour Jada Toys (Chub City, Dub City, Import Racer, Big Time Muscle) et a créé la ligne JL Full Throttle. Il est également crédité d'avoir supervisé le redesign de la marque Johnny Lightning. Il a ensuite été employé chez Wicked Cool Toys en tant que directeur senior du design. Il est actuellement employé chez Ultra Cornhole en tant que designer de vêtements et a sa propre entreprise, ET Design.

Dwayne Vance.biografia_limpia: Dwayne Alton Vance es Fundador y Diseñador Jefe de Future Elements. Su trabajo se puede ver en el renderizado de un hot rod, un boceto de un auto conceptual futurista, o de una lista de autos Hot Wheels diseñados. Vance, que fundó la empresa después de 8 años trabajando en la industria del diseño con empresas como Mattel Hot Wheels y Troy Lee Designs, tiene un título en Diseño Automotriz del prestigioso Art Center College of Design en Pasadena, CA. Trabajó en Hot Wheels de 2002 a 2005 y fue el diseñador principal de AcceleRacers; regresó a Mattel como Líder de Diseño para Hot Wheels en octubre de 2019. Actualmente actúa como Gerente de Diseño, cargo que ha ocupado desde marzo de 2021.

Brendon Vetuskey.biografia_limpia: Brendon Vetuskey es un diseñador de Hot Wheels que trabaja en Mattel desde 2007. Inicialmente trabajó en el departamento de Pistas y Playsets, ayudando a desarrollar la línea Trick Tracks, el Super Six Lane Raceway, fue diseñador principal de Monster Jam durante algunos años, así como gestionó el equipo de Entretenimiento; actualmente es el diseñador principal de los vehículos Red Line Club. A pesar de haber diseñado vehículos desde 2010, Brendon solo se transfirió al departamento de diseño en 2016. Varios autos personales de Brendon se han convertido en diseños de Hot Wheels, destacando el Custom '67 Pontiac Firebird. A pesar de haber trabajado en Mattel desde 2007, la participación de Brendon con Hot Wheels se remonta a 1998, cuando diseñó los Scream Machines para Kiddesigns. Antes de trabajar en Mattel, trabajó en Jakks Pacific.

Brendon Vetuskey.bio_en: Brendon J. Vetuskey is a Hot Wheels designer who has been working at Mattel since 2007. He initially worked in the Track and Playsets department, helping develop the Trick Tracks line, the Super Six Lane Raceway, lead Monster Jam designer for a few years, as well as managed the Entertainment team; he is currently the lead designer for the Red Line Club vehicles. Despite having designed vehicles since 2010, Brendon only transferred into the design department in 2016. A number of Brendon's own cars have been turned into Hot Wheels designs, notably the Custom '67 Pontiac Firebird, with releases of the '57 Plymouth Fury, '55 Chevy Bel Air Gasser and '84 Pontiac Firebird also being inspired by his personal vehicles. Despite only having worked at Mattel since 2007, Brendon's involvement with Hot Wheels stretches to 1998, when he designed the Scream Machines for Kiddesigns. Prior to working at Mattel, he worked at Jakks Pacific.

Andrés Andrieu.biografia_limpia: Andrés Andrieu (read as "ahn-drehs") is a graphic designer who has worked at Mattel since 2022. Born in Los Angeles, Andrés grew up fascinated by transportation, especially cars. He studied Studio Arts with a concentration in Graphic Design at Loyola Marymount University and also worked on transportation design at the Art Center College of Design at night. He started his own clothing brand in senior year, then worked as a graphic design intern at tokidoki, later recruited by WowWee toys. Currently on the graphics team for Hot Wheels working on RLC, Elite 64, Mattel Creations, NFTs, 5-Packs, multipacks, mystery models, special projects, Pull-Back Speeders, Super Rigs, Track Fleet, Character Cars and mainline cars. His first graphic design was the Preying Menace in the 2023 Mystery Models.

Ralph Benítez.biografia_limpia: Ralph M. Benítez is a Mexican-American Mattel employee who has been working with Mattel since 2013. Benítez initially did packaging design for various Mattel lines before joining the Hot Wheels team in 2016, doing graphic designs for various Hot Wheels cars; he currently works on "secret projects" and does graphics for Color Shifters, Super Rigs, Track Fleet, Silver Series and Pull-Back Speeders among other things. He was previously lead graphic designer on the Hot Wheels id series and a contributing designer on Virtual Garage products. Outside of his normal line of work, he is an electronic music producer whose works can be found on Soundcloud.

Kevin Geraldez.biografia_limpia: Kevin Geraldez is a Hot Wheels designer who has worked at Mattel since 2020. He specializes in graphic design and works on the Premium, RLC and Elite 64 lines alongside Steve Vandervate. Prior to working at Mattel, he was a graphic designer at various toy companies, including some competing brands such as Jada Toys, Maisto and Jakks Pacific. Geraldez's first graphic design was the Initial D-exclusive Toyota AE86 Sprinter Trueno, and has also worked on other products such as the Kawa-Bug-A, 1975 Chevrolet Monte Carlo and the Car Culture Hyper Haulers series.

Anton Henggono.biografia_limpia: Anton Henggono is a graphic designer who has worked at Hot Wheels since 2022. Born and raised in Jakarta, Indonesia, he has been passionate about automotive and motorcycle design from a young age. A graphic design graduate from Trisakti University, Jakarta, Anton moved to Los Angeles in 2006 to further his career. In Los Angeles, Anton honed his skills working with various action sports companies, focusing primarily on helmet graphics. In 2022, he joined the Hot Wheels design team, where he has since contributed to a wide array of projects, including mainline and special edition die-cast cars, as well as NFTs. Beyond his work with Hot Wheels, Anton is a seasoned custom painter, with a portfolio that includes helmets, motorcycles and automobiles. His first graphic design for Hot Wheels was the '15 Mazda MX-5 Miata (HKH87) released in the 2023 mainline.

Michael Heralda.biografia_limpia: Michael O. Heralda is a longtime graphic designer at Mattel who retired in June, in the summer of 2015. Prior to joining the Mattel group, Michael Heralda was Art Director at Kransco/Wham-O Toys in San Gabriel, CA for eight years. He started at Mattel in 1997 with the responsibility of designing graphics for the 1998 Hot Wheels product line. The very first Hot Wheels car Michael designed graphics for was the (#1 of 48) 1998 First Edition Ford Escort Rally. During his eight years with Hot Wheels, Mike has created over 2,500 (produced) Hot Wheels decorations as of 2005. In 2005, Michael was offered the opportunity to work on the Matchbox diecast brand, and he continued until June 2015 creating graphics for Matchbox vehicles. Adding another 1,700 Matchbox decorations to his Hot Wheels library, the original count of his works has grown to about 4,200 die cast vehicle decorations in all.

Bruce Schultz.biografia_limpia: Bruce Schultz is an independent contractor who worked with Mattel from 1994 to 2015. He is the owner of Bodylines, a design company. Schultz's company was responsible for the creation of many of the paint master prototypes as well as the "poster shoot" models of the castings that were to be put into production. He also did artwork for some of the 100% Hot Wheels sets, such as the American Graffiti 2-Car Set.

Mike Vasquez.biografia_limpia: Michael Vasquez is a Hot Wheels designer working at Mattel since 2022. He specializes in graphic design, with his current role being a product and package designer for Mattel; he is known to work on graphics for the Hot Wheels Skate and Hot Wheels RacerVerse series. He is known for his comic book illustrations, particularly of Rick & Morty, having worked as a graphic designer for numerous companies in the past.

Miq Willmott.biografia_limpia: Miq Willmott, stylized miQ WillmOtt, joined the Hot Wheels design team in 1999 as a Graphic Designer. He came from the record industry where he designed many T-shirts and album covers as well as being recognized as an accomplished artist. Willmott's style quickly spread throughout the line and soon he was promoted to Manager of the Graphics group. Miq was a leader in making sure every vehicle got some type of graphic after seeing that some of the cars that clogged the pegs appeared bare. As of 2001-2002 almost every car, even First Editions / New Models, which previously had less deco than segment series and repaint cars, has gotten a graphic boost. Hot Wheels graphics evolved as well under Miq. They got more complex as he pushed the boundaries of what could be executed with a tampo machine. Willmott left Hot Wheels in 2006, moving to Portland and opening his own design studio, TWEEQIM, with wife Thuy. They still consult for Hot Wheels designing graphics and elements that make their way onto many cars.
